In this passage, we will look at the sizing of a gravity settler that is intended to remove sand from a process stream, and we will see how the required plan area is arrived at. The settler needs a plan area of 196 m2, based on a throughput of 104 m3 h-1 together with a design overflow rate of 0.53 m h-1. It is worth bearing in mind that the overflow rate can be understood as the throughput divided by the plan area, so the area follows from the throughput and the rate taken together: at the stated rate, each square metre of plan area passes 0.53 m3 h-1, and the stated throughput accordingly sets the area at 196 m2.

A helpful dimensional check can also be applied to the sizing, providing further reassurance about the result. A throughput expressed in m3 h-1, divided by an overflow rate expressed in m h-1, gives an area in m2, and the stated values do indeed return the stated area. It should also be noted that no other quantity enters into the sizing at this stage: the area is fixed by the two stated values and by nothing else in the design.

Turning to the basis of the rate, this is a vendor rule for this solid, which is a point that deserves careful attention. No settling test on the actual slurry has been run, which means that the overflow rate cannot be regarded as a measured property of the material that the settler will actually treat. The plan area of 196 m2 therefore holds on that basis: while the arithmetic is exact for the stated rate, the rate itself rests on the vendor rule rather than on a test of the actual slurry. Any design that needs the rate to be confirmed would need the settling test first, and the sizing as stated does not include that confirmation.

Overall, then, the settler enters the design at 196 m2 of plan area, sized on a vendor overflow rate of 0.53 m h-1 for a throughput of 104 m3 h-1, with the test on the actual slurry still outstanding. It is, in the end, a sizing figure: it settles the area that the design carries forward, while settling nothing about how the settler will perform in service.
